author: south middlesex times
title: Rep. Frank Pallone criticizes GOP votes and addresses Trump-Epstein allegations
text:
Rep. Frank Pallone, who has represented New Jersey’s 6th district in the U.S. Congress since 1988, used his social media platform this week to criticize Republican colleagues and former President Donald Trump, focusing on health care costs, congressional activity, and recent allegations involving Jeffrey Epstein.
On November 11, Pallone posted: “They go on TV and talk like moderates. They go back home and sound reasonable. But then they go to the floor of the House and vote like extremists. Here’s a hot tip: Tom Kean and Jeff Van Drew will vote again to increase your health care costs this week.”
The following day, he commented on House Republican leadership: “It’s DAY 43 of the REPUBLICAN RETREAT. Mike Johnson just ended the longest Republican vacation in history so he could join Senate Republicans in selling out the American people. I’m not playing along—I’m a NO.” This post was made on November 12.
Later that same day, Pallone addressed allegations concerning Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein: “Trump KNEW Epstein was trafficking girls—according to new reporting, he even spent HOURS with them. What are Trump’s rubber-stamp Republicans helping him cover up? Vote 218 on the Epstein discharge petition is coming TODAY.”
Pallone has been a member of Congress for over three decades after replacing James J. Howard in 1988 and previously served in the New Jersey Senate from 1984 to 1988. Born in Long Branch, New Jersey in 1951, Pallone graduated from Middlebury College with a BA in 1973 and earned a JD from Rutgers University-Camden in 1978.
